message.reasoning_content:
We need to compare two statements. Both are from same actor (IBAMA president). Manifestation A is a public hearing about oil exploration in Equatorial Margin near Amazon mouth. He explains IBAMA's technical analysis, says they haven't said never authorize, they denied some blocks, need more studies, etc. He emphasizes technical decision, not political, and that they will say yes when viability shown.

Manifestation B is a minister appearance (maybe before Congress) about veto of IBAMA to license for Petrobras to drill in Foz do Amazonas and other issues. He says IBAMA is biggest client of Petrobras, many licenses issued, currently analyzing 110 processes outside Equatorial Margin, 15 in Equatorial Margin. He mentions specific licenses granted in Potiguar basin.

We need to see if they respond to same specific proposition. Proposition likely: "Should IBAMA grant license for Petrobras to drill in Foz do Amazonas (Block 59)?" In A, he explains why license not granted yet, technical issues, need more studies, but not a final stance? He says "Toda vez que houver viabilidade, o IBAMA vai dizer 'sim'. Toda vez que, no processo, não houver viabilidade, contem com o 'não' do IBAMA." He indicates currently not viable, so stance is against granting now. In B, he is responding to questions about the veto; he says they are analyzing 15 processes in Equatorial Margin, but doesn't explicitly state stance on the specific veto. He mentions they are biggest client, many licenses granted, but not directly addressing the specific veto decision. He says "Em relação aos questionamentos dos Deputados ... sobre as licenças da PETROBRAS, nós brincamos ... que ela é a maior cliente ... emitimos 173 licenças ... estamos analisando hoje 110 processos ... 15 processos na Margem Equatorial." He doesn't say they will grant or deny the specific license. So the two statements are about same general topic (Petrobras licensing in Equatorial Margin) but not the same specific proposition (granting license for Block 59). A addresses that specific case; B is more general about licensing workload. So they are not responding to same specific proposition. Both have determinable positions? A has a stance (currently not granting). B doesn't express stance on that specific proposition. So relation: INCOMPARABLE? But criteria: INCOMPARABLE: both have determinable position but not same proposition. Here B may not have determinable position on that specific proposition. Could be RELATION_UNCERTAIN because comparability unclear. However definition: RELATION_UNCERTAIN: some step (determinability, comparability, stance) not sufficiently clear. Since B doesn't clearly express stance on same proposition, comparability uncertain. I'd choose RELATION_UNCERTAIN.

But check INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE: at least one manifestation doesn't present determinable position on any specific proposition. B does present position on licensing workload but not on specific proposition. However it does present a position (they are analyzing many processes). That's a position on a proposition "Are there many pending licenses?" That's determinable. But the question is about same specific proposition. Since they are not same, INCOMPARABLE requires both have determinable position but different propositions. B does have determinable position (they are analyzing 15 processes). So both have determinable positions but different propositions => INCOMPARABLE.

Thus answer: INCOMPARABLE. Reasoning: A addresses specific license decision for Block 59, stating technical denial; B discusses overall licensing statistics and ongoing analyses, not the same specific proposition.
